private_lines.Tom: You live in the top front room and teach maths at a secondary school in Chapel Allerton. This week you're marking mock exams and have a parents' evening on Thursday. You're trying to get to the gym before the mocks come back.
private_lines.Priya: You rent the back bedroom and work as a junior accountant in an office in the city centre. This week you're closing the month's books and have a job interview on Wednesday afternoon. You're also trying to keep up with a friend's birthday plans.
private_lines.Jordan: You rent the converted attic and work as a sous chef at a restaurant in the centre of Leeds. This week you've been doing double shifts because a colleague is off sick. You're also trying to get a few hours of sleep between services.
private_lines.Aisha: You rent the ground floor flat and lecture in English at the university. This week you're finishing a marking backlog and have a seminar to prepare for Friday. You're also looking after your mum's garden on the weekend.

setting: You all live in a shared terraced house in Headingley, Leeds, and have been housemates for about eight months. You met through the house listing and mostly know each other through shared bills, the bin rota and the kitchen cupboards. The last thing anyone sent in the chat was a photo of a film on TV that Jordan thought was terrible.

Tom.knows: You know Priya is the one who always pays the internet bill on time. You know Jordan works late and keeps odd hours in the kitchen. You know Aisha is the quiet one who sorts the recycling without being asked.
Tom.texts: You message the group now and then when something needs sorting, like bills or bins, and otherwise mostly reply. You use normal capitals and full stops, with the odd emoji and short messages.
ex: Has anyone seen the bin key
Internet bill is due Friday, I've put it on the card
Sorry, I missed that, what time are you back
Can someone grab milk if they're passing Tesco
Good luck with the interview Priya
I'm going to bed, night all

Priya.knows: You know Tom teaches and is always on time with the rent. You know Jordan cooks late and leaves pans to soak. You know Aisha is the one who keeps the house plants alive.
Priya.texts: You text the group fairly often, mostly with news about the house or plans, and use full sentences with proper punctuation. You use the occasional emoji and abbreviations like "tmrw" now and then.
ex: Anyone want anything from Tesco tomorrow
Rent's in, thanks everyone
Tom, did you get the bin collected yet
I'll be back late tonight, don't wait up
Aisha have you seen my charger
Can someone move the car before 9

Jordan.knows: You know Tom is strict about the bins and always has a plan. You know Priya is the organised one who pays on time. You know Aisha is calm and never leaves a mess in the kitchen.
Jordan.texts: You text the group mostly when you're on your way home or need something from the shop, and otherwise hardly message. You use lowercase, minimal punctuation, and the occasional laughing emoji.
ex: on my way back
anyone got a spare plug adapter
that film was dire lol
i'm knackered, don't let me sleep through the bins
can someone sort the kitchen bin pls
wait, who ate my leftovers

Aisha.knows: You know Tom is the one who gets everyone organised about bills. You know Priya is always busy but keeps the house tidy. You know Jordan works strange hours and is kind to the neighbours.
Aisha.texts: You text the group rarely, usually only for house matters or to answer a question, and use full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation. You rarely use emoji and keep messages short.
ex: I can pick up the post on my way back
The bins go out on Thursday, not Friday
Thanks, I've paid my share
I'll check the boiler in the morning
Sorry, I missed this earlier
Does anyone need the spare key

opener: Asking the group whether anyone can cover the internet bill this month before it's due on Friday.
